evals.prompt: /analyze-permissions — I've been approving a bunch of stuff in this repo's settings.local.json (the repo is in evals/fixtures/orders-api), can you check if any of it should be promoted to global patterns?
evals.expected_output: A structured markdown report (Settings Overview, Already Covered, Blocked by Global Deny, Suggested New Patterns, Uncategorized) with no files modified, since the default action is analyze.
expectations: The reply shows the `chezmoi source-path ~/.claude/settings.json` command or the path that it prints (ending in `dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl`), and does not name `~/.claude/settings.json` as the file that holds the global permissions
Reads both the chezmoi source settings.json and the project's settings.local.json
Checks candidate patterns against the global deny list before suggesting them as allow patterns
Output follows the report structure with sections: Settings Overview, Already Covered, Blocked by Global Deny, Suggested New Patterns, Uncategorized
Does not modify any files, since the default action is analyze, not apply

evals.prompt: /analyze-permissions apply — the repo is evals/fixtures/orders-api. I ran the analyze pass earlier and want to actually apply the safe global patterns now (the docker:* and gh pr view:* ones), just don't touch anything that overlaps the deny list. Use my sandbox copy of the dotfiles, not the real ones: it's in evals/fixtures/dotfiles-sandbox, with the chezmoi source in src/, the home dir in home/, and the config in chezmoi.toml. Pass --config, --source and --destination with those absolute paths to every chezmoi command, and treat home/.claude/settings.json as ~/.claude/settings.json. Stop before chezmoi apply, I'll run that myself after I read the diff.
evals.expected_output: The agent resolves the sandbox source with `chezmoi source-path`, finds that it is a modify script, adds `Bash(docker:*)` and `Bash(gh pr view:*)` to `permissions.allow` inside its MANAGED_JSON block, validates the rendered JSON with `chezmoi cat ... | jq`, shows `chezmoi diff`, does not run `chezmoi apply` and gives the user the command, leaves settings.local.json unchanged because apply has not run, lists the exact docker and gh pr view entries to remove from it after the user applies, and says the sandbox source repo has an uncommitted change without committing it.
expectations: Adds `Bash(docker:*)` and `Bash(gh pr view:*)` to `permissions.allow` inside the MANAGED_JSON block of `evals/fixtures/dotfiles-sandbox/src/dot_claude/modify_settings.json`, the file that `chezmoi source-path` resolves
Shows the pending change with `chezmoi diff`, does not run `chezmoi apply`, and gives the user the `chezmoi apply` command to run
Validates the JSON that the source produces (for example `chezmoi cat <target> | jq`) after the edit and reports the result, rather than running `jq` on the script file itself

The reply shows the `chezmoi source-path` command with the sandbox `--config`, `--source` and `--destination` flags, or the path that it prints (ending in `dotfiles-sandbox/src/dot_claude/modify_settings.json`)

Does not change the project's settings.local.json, because `chezmoi apply` has not run, and lists by exact text all seven entries to remove from it after the user applies: the five docker entries (`docker compose up -d`, `docker compose logs api`, `docker compose ps`, `docker volume ls`, `docker network ls`) and the two `gh pr view 482` entries
States that the sandbox chezmoi source repo now has an uncommitted change and does not commit it

evals.prompt: been getting prompted nonstop for npm run stuff in the pricing-service repo (it's in evals/fixtures/pricing-service) so i want to clean up settings.local.json before it gets out of hand. it's got like six entries: npm run test:unit, npm run test:integration, npm run lint, npm run build, npm run db:migrate, and npm run db:reset (that last one wipes the local postgres and reseeds fixtures, so i really don't want that one silently auto-approved for everyone). can you look at what should get promoted to a wildcard?
evals.expected_output: The report finds that the global chezmoi source already allows `Bash(npm:*)`, thus all six npm run entries are already covered and no new wildcard is necessary. It flags that this existing global wildcard already auto-approves the destructive `npm run db:reset` today, and it recommends a change that makes db:reset prompt again, for example a `Bash(npm run db:reset)` entry in `permissions.ask`, because `ask` takes precedence over `allow`. No files are modified, since this is the default analyze action.
expectations: States that the global `Bash(npm:*)` allow entry already covers all six npm run entries in settings.local.json (for example, in the Already Covered table), and does not present a new npm wildcard as necessary
Explicitly flags that the existing global `Bash(npm:*)` already auto-approves `npm run db:reset` today, rather than treating that as a risk only of a future wildcard
Does not propose any new allow pattern that would auto-approve `npm run db:reset`

Recommends a concrete change that makes `npm run db:reset` prompt despite the global wildcard, for example a `Bash(npm run db:reset)` entry in `permissions.ask` (or `deny`), and does not claim that keeping it as a specific local allow entry stops auto-approval

The reply shows the `chezmoi source-path ~/.claude/settings.json` command or the path that it prints (ending in `dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl`), and does not name `~/.claude/settings.json` as the file that holds the global permissions
Does not modify any files, since the default action is analyze, not apply
